Welcome to new member Phil Lovell who has already set a new Club PV record of 4.75m. Phil will be eligible to compete for us in the 3rd British League Match.

…h a few of our younger members participating in sub-zero Open Meetings (and producing a spate of personal best's) while Phil Lovell, Colin Gaynor and Stu Paton have taken time out for indoor competition with Phil setting a new Club polevault record and Stu winning the AAA's indoor 1500m Championship…
Colin Gaynor showed early season form by running 12th fastest in the 60m while new signing Phil Lovell set a club polevault record with 4.50m to clinch 8th spot .
In the field events new member Phil Lovell's 4.70 was good enough to put him 10th in the pole vault with Mark Shippen's 4.30 being good enough for 30th.
In the Senior ranks Phil Lovell pushed his p.b. and our Pole Vault record to 4.75m at a S.Counties,Loughborough Univ.,London Univ.,Civil Service match held at West London on Wed. 27th April.

By the season's end 2 Vets records had been broken by Charlie Gillett and Bill Treharne; 7 Senior records had been either broken or equalled by John Gladwin, Mark L Bayley, Jim Gregg, Phil Lovell Derek Williams, Ken Onuagaluchi and the 4x400m squad of Guy Sagar, John Gladwin, Stuart Paton, and Dave Mote.
Jim Gregg made his first appearance this year in the high jump and Phil Lovell despite injury popped over in the pole vault to gain valuable points.
In the Senior events Derrick Williams won the long jump in slippery conditions with 7.08, while Phil Lovell gained silver in the pole vault with 4.60 and Mark Shippen finished in 6th place with 4.20.
Ken triumphed in the discus again confirming that he is now pushing International class, Phil Lovell won the discus and John Bicourt returned to the chase and recorded a fine 9.28.4.
SOUTHERN CHAMPIONSHIPS-COPTHALL-17/18 JUNE-PHIL LOVELL SILVER Phil Lovell was our only medallist at the Southern, vaulting 4.60 behind Keith Stock's CBP of 5.21.
Mark has been a consistant and prolific points scorer in our British League matches and he and Phil Lovell form a very formidable partnership for next season.

Ken Onuaguluchi, Phil Lovell, Mark Shippen, Aham Amadi and Derrick Williams added respectability to the field events while in the middle distance, Stu Paton won the 400 and John Gladwin got outkicked by a certain Steve Crabb!

Dave Armstrong's blocks slipped in the 100, Phil Lovell fell foul of an over zealous judge and the weather in the pole vault and failed his opening height, and John Aska despite a dash by taxi just missed the hammer.
